rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a 3BB blastocyst, but it overstates visibility of a distinct ICM and calls the embryo 'good quality'; the image shows an expanded blastocyst with thin zona and relatively sparse/loose TE, while some claimed detail is not clearly discernible.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve markers, sperm parameters, endometrium, prior cycle history, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis. It appropriately emphasizes young age, though it somewhat overinterprets the DOR label conflict.

Reasoning is generally structured and internally consistent, but the implantation estimate is somewhat optimistic for an untested 3BB embryo and there is mild tension between calling morphology merely 'good' versus assigning a very high probability.

SET recommendation and general counseling are guideline-concordant, but suggesting ERA after a single failed transfer and implying FET may have higher implantation in general are not strongly guideline-supported; PGT-A after one failed transfer in a 29-year-old is also more debatable than standard.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, and future evaluation options. Some recommendations are somewhat generic or premature, but overall clinically usable.
